name: Teman
overview: Teman was a male Edomite, recognized as the son of Eliphaz and a chief among the Edomites. His identity is grounded in his lineage and leadership role within the Edomite tribe. There are no additional notes expanding on his character beyond these attributes.
namesAndTitles: The name Teman means 'on the right [not left] side,' reflecting a proper name given in the Hebrew context. This meaning is noted in Genesis 36:11 but was not given by God directly.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Teman as the son of Eliphaz, establishing his place within the Edomite genealogy. No other family relationships are documented beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Teman holds significance as a prominent figure in the Edomite lineage, both as a son of Eliphaz and as a chief of Edom. His mention in Genesis 36 underscores the structured leadership and tribal organization among the Edomites, highlighting the continuity of Eliphaz's descendants in positions of authority.
